neighbours.label: a spatial or relational preposition placing something relative to a place or boundary (along, within, away from, close to, above)
fire: Hikers reported seeing bears along the trail near the lake.
Investigators found evidence of fraud within the company's finance office.
The family lives far away from the nearest hospital.
The new houses were built close to the river bank.
Fishing boats were spotted along the northern coast this week.
Rangers placed warning signs along the edge of the cliff.
Engineers detected small cracks within the concrete walls.
The soldiers camped just below the ridge overnight.
quiet: Hikers reported seeing two bears late last week.
Investigators found evidence of fraud after a long audit.
The family waited three hours for the doctor to arrive.
The new houses were built in less than a year.
Fishing boats returned late this week after the storm.
Rangers replaced the warning signs every spring.
Engineers finished the repairs within a single day.
The soldiers rested for most of the night.

notes: Broad pole (2.4%). Probe: 'along the highway' 0.96, 'without damaging' 0.67, 'far away from' 0.62, 'spies within' 0.62, 'close to the border' 0.51, 'above the ocean' 0.48, 'on the sofa' 0.28. Temporal 'within an hour' 0.03 and partitive 'part of' 0.08 (the + pole's side) were low. Near misses keep the topic and use temporal phrasing or no preposition.
